purpose: Selects the smallest of the three predefined integration-grid schemes; grid sizes close to older ORCA defaults but with improved robustness.
defaults: default scheme is DEFGRID2; DEFGRID1 must be requested
typical_use: quick large calculations; turning the default DEFGRID2 down when speed matters more than grid error
note: XC grid AngularGrid 3 / COSX 1,1,2 for SCF per Table 2.48

purpose: The default ORCA 6 integration-grid scheme; benchmarked to keep DFT grid errors around 0.01 kcal/mol, so it is adequate for most work.
defaults: default since ORCA 5.0 (XC AngularGrid 4 / COSX 1,2,3, Table 2.48)
typical_use: the standard choice; upgrade to DEFGRID3 for the cases listed in manual 2.10.7
literature: ref 120 (the grid-scheme publication cited in manual 2.9)

purpose: The largest predefined grid scheme; very large and conservative, built to keep energy errors well below the default scheme's.
typical_use: anions with charge below -3, very subtle intermolecular interactions, unusual electronic structures, large conjugated systems, or when an error below ~0.2 kcal/mol is required
note: XC grid AngularGrid 6 / COSX 2,3,4 for SCF per Table 2.48

purpose: Requests the reference-quality grid for energy benchmarks; not described in the 6.1 manual text, so the record stays minimal.

purpose: Requests a rotationally invariant grid construction; not described in the 6.1 manual text, so the record stays minimal.

purpose: Sets the Lebedev angular-grid scheme (1-7, or 0 for a Gauss-Legendre grid) for the XC integration; 1-5 points regions and IntAcc control radial density.

purpose: Controls the number of radial grid points via the IntAcc value; each unit adds 15 radial points per atom.
opi: none (no OPI enum or block field)
defaults: set by the DEFGRID scheme (XC 4.004 / COSX 4.020 for AngularGrid 2, Table 2.47)

purpose: Raises the radial accuracy (IntAcc) for selected atoms only; the manual notes it is rarely needed any more because the basis is considered in grid construction.

purpose: Sets the XC and COSX grids used in the CP-SCF step (response equations); IntAcc values 3.467 (XC) and 3.067 (COSX) are smaller than the SCF ones by design.
opi: none (no OPI enum or block field)

purpose: Chooses the grid-pruning scheme; default is adaptive pruning which detects core polarization and diffuse functions, OLDPRUNING is the pre-5.0 scheme, UNPRUNED removes pruning.
opi: none (no OPI enum or block field)

purpose: Activates Grimme's D3 dispersion correction with Becke-Johnson damping; per the manual !D3 and !D3BJ are equivalent and BJ damping is generally recommended.
pairs_with: a DFT/HF functional that has D3(BJ) parameters (HF is only parameterized with BJ damping)
defaults: BJ damping; D3 available for elements up to Pu (Z=94)
typical_use: almost every DFT calculation; dispersion corrections are almost always recommended per manual 3.4 intro
literature: Grimme, S.; Antony, J.; Ehrlich, S.; Krieg, H. J. Chem. Phys., 2010, 132, 154104; Grimme, S.; Ehrlich, S.; Goerigk, L. J. Comput. Chem., 2011, 32, 1456

purpose: Activates the D3 correction with zero damping instead of Becke-Johnson damping; required for functionals (like M06) that are only parameterized with zero damping.
excludes: not parameterized for all functionals (HF has no zero-damped parameters)
note: D30 is the equivalent spelling the manual lists in Table 3.13

purpose: Activates special D3 damping parameters optimized for the def2-TZVPP triple-zeta basis set; only available together with zero damping.
typical_use: triple-zeta calculations where the default D3 parameters are fitted for double-zeta-quality results; results slightly worse than QZ with defaults per ref 272 SI

purpose: Activates the D4 dispersion correction (atomic-charge-dependent polarizabilities) with Becke-Johnson damping and the three-body (ATM) term included by default; the generally recommended variant.
defaults: BJ damping and ATM three-body term on by default; D4 available up to Lr (Z=103)
typical_use: recommended default dispersion correction for modern functionals; r2SCAN-3c and PWPB95-class work
literature: Grimme group D4 papers cited in the manual's dispersion section (refs 159, 274); actinide extension: Wittmann et al. Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 2024, 26, 21379-21394

purpose: Activates the older D2 dispersion correction; kept for compatibility, superseded by D3 and D4.
note: listed in Table 3.13 without a dedicated section; the manual treats D1/D2 as deprecated via DFTDOPT 1/2

purpose: Activates the three-body (Axilrod-Teller-Muto) dispersion term for D3-type corrections; D4 already includes it by default.
typical_use: supramolecular thermochemistry where the three-body term improves accuracy (ref 280)

purpose: Activates the non-self-consistent VV10 non-local dispersion correction (DFT-NL): a post-SCF evaluation of the VV10 kernel on the converged density.
excludes: TD-DFT with NL not available; second-derivative (Hessian/polarizability) use not available; self-consistent NL not possible with HF
pairs_with: functionals with implemented b parameters (Table 3.18: B3LYP, PBE, TPSS, B97M-V, WB97X-V, ...)
typical_use: metallic systems or when the electronic structure changes strongly (ionization/oxidation), where NL is preferred over D3/D4
literature: Vydrov and Van Voorhis VV10 (ref 275); evaluation ref 276 (GMTKN30/S66); vdW-DF: Langreth and Lundqvist (ref 282)

purpose: Activates the self-consistent variant of the VV10 NL correction, where orbitals and density are optimized with the full DFT+VV10 potential; rarely necessary for normal energies.
